cards.headline: Lyrics born from drunken chaos in Oxford
cards.snippet: Radiohead first played an early version of the song, then called "Open Pick", on their 2006 tour. Singer Thom Yorke based the lyrics on the chaos he saw while drinking in Oxford. He called them quite caustic, about drinking yourself into oblivion to forget. He said there is partly elation in it, but a much darker side too. The song later opened the In Rainbows era as a single in January 2008.
cards.context: The song began life as 'Open Pick' on Radiohead's 2006 tour.

cards.headline: David Byrne asked if the helmets would be cut
cards.snippet: In 2007, Adam Buxton and Garth Jennings made the video for Radiohead's "Jigsaw Falling Into Place" in the band's studio, using cameras on silver bike helmets. David Byrne was visiting, watched an early edit and asked whether the helmets would be cut. Buxton said no, because the helmets looking ridiculous was the point. He said the band committed to the idea and performed it brilliantly. He admits fans rate it among the least popular Radiohead videos, but he counts it among his best work.
cards.context: Buxton calls it perhaps the least popular Radiohead video with fans, yet one of his best works.

cards.headline: Radiohead's live debut, when the song was still called 'Open Pick'
